A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dengue fever control discourse in Malaysia has been dominated by a biomedical discourse which has been transferred to Malaysia from the West and has been used as a means for the control of the disease.
we need to understand that there are different types of diseases that are associated with poverty and that there are different approaches that are needed for the different diseases.
the discourse of poverty and the poor as the cause and the target of NTDs has been used as an excuse to ignore the real causes of NTDs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the global discourse on dengue fever is not a neutral description of the disease but is a political and moral discourse that has the potential to influence public health policy and practice in ways that are inappropriate to particular local contexts.

global health discourse can be an important driver of health policy and practice at the local level, and that the critical examination of such discourse is a key strategy in developing locally appropriate health policies.
global health policy transfer is not always appropriate or effective, and that the transfer of hegemonic discourses and strategies to non hegemonic environments may lead to unintended outcomes.
